health.title: Backup health
health.description: Every backed up database and app volume, grouped by app. A backup only counts once a restore of it has been proven to work.
health.empty: No backed up resources yet. Schedule or trigger a backup from a database's or app volume's own page.
health.drillStartedDescription: It restores into a scratch resource, validates it and destroys it. Results appear in the drill history.
health.drillFailedToast: Could not start the restore drill

encryption.on: New volume backups are compressed and encrypted on this server before upload. Public key: {{key}}
encryption.off: New volume backups are compressed but not encrypted. Anyone with bucket access can read them.
encryption.keyHint: Keep a copy of the key file (APP_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE, default backup-encryption.key in the data directory) somewhere off this server, or encrypted backups cannot be restored after a disaster.

protection.title: Bucket protection
protection.checkFailed: Could not probe the backup buckets
protection.open: Anyone with the key can delete backups

restoreWizard.title: Restore {{app}}/{{volume}}
restoreWizard.description: Restores always go into a new volume. The existing volume is never overwritten.
restoreWizard.noBackups: There is no succeeded backup of this volume to restore.
restoreWizard.sameApp: A new volume next to the original
restoreWizard.otherApp: A new volume for another app
restoreWizard.targetAppHint: The volume is named so that deploying this app mounts the restored data.
restoreWizard.summary: Restore backup {{backup}} into a new volume {{name}} on {{node}}.
restoreWizard.startedDescription: Follow progress in the restore history of this volume.

policy.title: Backup policy for {{app}}/{{volume}}
policy.description: Retention counts keep the newest backup of each of the last N days, weeks and months. Hooks run inside the app container.
policy.retentionHint: 0 turns a bucket off. Counts combine with the schedule's own keep-last and age limits.
policy.preHookHint: A non-zero exit fails the backup, so an inconsistent volume is never archived.
policy.pause: Pause the app while the archive streams
policy.pauseHint: Freezes every process in the container so files cannot change mid-archive. The app is unavailable until the upload finishes.
policy.failed: Could not save the backup policy
policy.loadFailed: Could not load the backup policy: {{error}}

drills.title: Restore drills
drills.description: Scheduled and manual restores into scratch resources. A failed drill raises the restore_drill_failed alert.
drills.empty: No drills have run yet. Drills run automatically once a week by default.
drills.shortDescription: Restores into scratch resources prove a backup works.

history.title: All backup attempts
history.description: Every attempt across every database and app volume, newest first.

page.title: Backups
page.description: What is protected, what is not, and one place to fix it.
page.noResourcesDescription: Databases and app volumes show up here as soon as you create them.

headline.empty: No databases or app volumes yet.
headline.allVerified: Every resource is backed up and a restore has been proven.
headline.failing: Backups are failing for {{failing}} of them. Fix those first.
headline.unverified: Backed up, but a restore has not been proven for every resource yet.

row.backupFailed: Could not start a backup of {{name}}

target.localWarning: Backups stored on this machine's own disk are lost with the machine. They protect against a bad deploy or a deleted table, not against a dead disk, a ransomware hit or a deleted server. Use this to try things out, then add an off-site destination.

protectAll.title: Protect everything
protectAll.description: Schedule a backup for every resource that has none. Nothing changes until you apply.
protectAll.includeScratch_one: Also protect {{count}} scratch resource (previews and canaries)
protectAll.includeScratch_other: Also protect {{count}} scratch resources (previews and canaries)
protectAll.nothingToDo: Every resource already has a schedule.

safety.title: Encryption and bucket safety
safety.copyFailed: Could not copy the public key
safety.keyHint: Keep the private key (APP_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE, default backup-encryption.key in the data directory) in a password manager or another machine. Without it, encrypted backups cannot be restored after a disaster.
safety.keyNotStored: You have not confirmed that the private key is stored off this server. If this server is lost, so are these backups.
safety.ack: I stored it off this server

orphans.title: Orphaned data
orphans.description: Data kept after its database or app was deleted. Deleting a database never removes its data by itself, so nothing here is removed until you reclaim it.
orphans.empty: No orphaned data. Every volume belongs to a database or app that still exists.
orphans.large: Orphaned data uses {{size}}. Review it and reclaim what you no longer need.
orphans.noBackupDetail: No backup of this data exists
orphans.confirmDescription: The volume is deleted from this server. This cannot be undone.
orphans.confirmNoBackup: No backup of this data exists. It will be gone for good.
orphans.confirmHasBackup_one: {{count}} backup of it stays in your destination.
orphans.confirmHasBackup_other: {{count}} backups of it stay in your destination.

deleteData.label: Also delete the data
deleteData.databaseHint: Removes the data volume with the database. Without this, the volume is kept and listed under Orphaned data on the Backups page.
deleteData.appHint: Removes the app's volumes with the app. Without this, they are kept and listed under Orphaned data on the Backups page.
deleteData.warning: The data is destroyed and cannot be recovered unless a backup exists.

firstRun.title: Set up backups
firstRun.description: Connect somewhere safe to keep backups, and every database and app volume can be protected from there.
firstRun.descriptionWithResources_one: {{count}} resource has no backup. Connect somewhere safe to keep them, then protect it in one step.
firstRun.descriptionWithResources_other: {{count}} resources have no backups. Connect somewhere safe to keep them, then protect them all in one step.

verify.title: Prove a restore
verify.hint: A backup counts once it restores

suggestion.title: Back this database up
suggestion.description: A destination is connected, but this database has no schedule. Suggested: {{schedule}}, keeping the last {{retain}}.

banner.description: Protect databases and volumes with scheduled backups to storage you control, then prove they restore.
